- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.30), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +3% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (last 3 days > +0.30), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 7 days.  
- Model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is negative and price is falling; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment < -0.40 and price > 65.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 10-day moving average is above 70 and sentiment is neutral, forecast should be capped at 70–72.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– > 0.20), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 5 days.
